notes: Scope: the snapshot is the whole ros2/rviz repository at version 7.0.4 (all built packages carry 7.0.4; rviz/ is the legacy tree marked AMENT_IGNORE/CATKIN_IGNORE and was excluded). The rviz2 package proper (snapshot/rviz2) contains only src/main.cpp, which builds rviz_common::VisualizerApp with a RosClientAbstraction (main.cpp:72-73), and a test tool publishing sensor_msgs/PointCloud on 'pointcloud'; it names none of the four packet elements itself. rviz2 exec_depends on rviz_default_plugins and depends on rviz_common (rviz2/package.xml:25,27), and the subscriptions to the packet message types are made by those packages' display plugins loaded into rviz2 at run time; the ports and references therefore describe the rviz2 application as assembled from this repository. api:rmw_create_subscription: no code in the snapshot names it; rviz reaches it only indirectly through rclcpp::Node::create_subscription (ros_topic_display.hpp:179, marker_display.cpp:75-76, map_display.cpp:216, camera_display.cpp:282) and message_filters::Subscriber (message_filter_display.hpp:119-122), so it is not in references and its port fields are null (no definition file exists for a C API symbol). topic:/test: the name is never written in the snapshot; display topic names come from the Topic property (default empty string, ros_topic_display.hpp:69) set at run time from the GUI or a .rviz configuration outside the snapshot, so it is in neither references nor declares; its message type depends on which display type is bound to it at run time (null). Its durability is null because it depends on that run-time display choice: volatile for displays using the base qos_profile(5), transient_local for RobotModelDisplay (robot_model_display.cpp:122). For all ports the reliability/durability values recorded are the code defaults; every _RosTopicDisplay exposes a QosProfileProperty (ros_topic_display.hpp:72, qos_profile_property.cpp:85-100) through which the user or a saved .rviz config can change Depth, History, Reliability and Durability at run time; deadline is never set in code. MarkerDisplay also subscribes visualization_msgs/MarkerArray on '<topic>_array' with the same QoS (marker_display.cpp:75-78). geometry_msgs/PoseStamped is additionally published by GoalTool on default topic 'goal' with header.frame_id set to the fixed frame (goal_tool.cpp:52,75,85); that is a use of the consumed message type, not a provided packet element. Definitions were fetched from ros2/common_interfaces tag 0.8.1, the highest 0.8.x (Eloquent series) tag that resolved (0.8.2 to 0.8.6 returned 404); definition_id values are sha256_normalised proxies over the top-level .msg text only (nested types not expanded). No element is provided by this package, so declares and not_declared are empty. Units left null: neither the code nor the top-level definitions state units for these ports (Marker.msg line 42 describes scale only as 'usually 1 meter square').
